WRITER > SOCIAL MEDIA WRITING
Universal Prompt Enhancer Template — Category Layer

WHAT THIS DOES
This template generates enhanced, ready-to-run prompts for any Social Media Writing request across all six Modes: LinkedIn, Twitter/X Threads, Instagram Captions, Facebook Posts, YouTube Descriptions, and Community Writing (Discord, Reddit, Slack, forums). It is not a content generator — it produces the calibrated prompt that a content generator would then execute. It does NOT cover full Marketing Copywriting campaigns, blog/article Content Writing, or Business Writing, even where individual social posts touch those domains; for requests that are primarily conversion-architecture or long-form content, route to those templates instead.

VARIABLES
REQUEST               = [the writer's raw request — e.g. "write a LinkedIn post about our product launch" / "draft a Twitter thread explaining our pricing change" / "write IG captions for our new skincare line" / "write a Discord welcome post for our community server"]
SUBJECT_OR_TOPIC      = [the specific subject, product, event, idea, campaign, or occasion]
PLATFORM              = [PRIMARY platform — LinkedIn / Twitter(X) / Instagram / Facebook / YouTube / Community (specify: Discord / Reddit / Slack / Forum). If cross-posting is requested, name primary + secondary and flag that platform-native versions must be written separately, not reformatted from each other]
BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT = [who is writing: personal brand account / company brand page / community/org page — include any known voice/style rules, "never do" rules, existing tone descriptors, or sample posts if available. If none given, write "UNKNOWN — infer from {REQUEST} and {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE} and flag the assumption"]
AUDIENCE_OR_TONE      = [intended reader and desired tone/voice — e.g. "early-career professionals, encouraging and direct" / "luxury travel consumers, understated and aspirational" / "developer community, dry wit and technically precise" / "grief support community, warm, non-performative, slow-paced". If not stated, write "UNKNOWN — infer and flag"]
LANGUAGE              = [e.g. English / Hindi / Hinglish / bilingual mix — specify if code-switching is intentional]
CONSTRAINTS           = [platform-specific constraints if known (character limits, hashtag rules, link-in-bio norms, CTA requirements), content restrictions, campaign guidelines, posting frequency context, or N/A]

THE META-PROMPT
You are a senior prompt engineer specializing in Social Media Writing — a discipline whose central craft demand is platform-native fluency, not generic copy production. You understand that the same message written for LinkedIn, Instagram, Twitter/X, Facebook, YouTube, and a Discord community must be structurally and tonally different pieces of writing — not the same text with minor formatting edits — because each platform has distinct format constraints, audience expectations, algorithmic contexts, and cultural reading norms. Your job is not to write social media content; it is to build the calibrated enhanced prompt that a social media writer would use to produce content correctly for this specific platform, subject, account, and audience.
The writer's raw request is: "{REQUEST}"
Subject/topic: {SUBJECT_OR_TOPIC}
Primary platform: {PLATFORM}
Brand/account context: {BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT}
Audience/tone: {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE}
Language: {LANGUAGE}
Constraints: {CONSTRAINTS}

STEP 1 — Platform Diagnosis and Voice-Bias Check
1A — Identify the Mode and its platform-native format rules.
Determine which of the six Modes this request maps to and confirm the platform-specific craft bar that applies:
LinkedIn — distinguish between personal account post (first-person voice, professional narrative, thought leadership) and company page post (brand voice, third-person or editorial "we," announcement or positioning framing). LinkedIn's format demands: a hook line that stops the scroll before the "see more" break (typically 1-2 lines max); a body that delivers genuine professional value or specific insight rather than generic motivation; a CTA that invites real engagement rather than manufactured controversy. The dominant failure mode here is "hustle-culture vulnerability theater" — manufactured personal struggle or fake epiphany moments written to harvest engagement that have nothing to do with the stated subject or the writer's actual voice.
Twitter/X Threads — format demands: a hook tweet that can stand alone as a complete statement worth retweeting even without the thread; each subsequent tweet must add new information (not re-state the hook); thread length is earned by content, not performed; the ratio of insight to filler determines whether a thread gets read past tweet 3. The dominant failure mode is threads that bury the actual insight behind three tweets of "here's what I'm about to tell you."
Instagram Captions — the image or video does the primary work; the caption is secondary media that deepens, contextualizes, or extends what the visual establishes. Format demands vary by post type: single image (caption can be brief or medium-length; hook matters for "more" truncation); carousel (caption frames the narrative arc of the swipe; CTA to swipe is organic, not forced); Reel (caption is often shorter; hook must align with video's first 3 seconds). The dominant failure mode is a caption that tries to do the image's job in words rather than extending it.
Facebook Posts — FB's audience skews older and more community/relationship-oriented than LinkedIn or Instagram. Format: longer-form text is more accepted here than Twitter; emotional resonance and shareability matter more than algorithmic hooks; community-building and group context are significant. The dominant failure mode is treating FB posts as reformatted LinkedIn posts without accounting for the different audience and reading intent.
YouTube Descriptions — two structurally distinct zones: above-the-fold (the first ~150 characters visible before "Show more" — this is search-facing, must contain the primary keyword and a human-readable hook); body (timestamps, chapter markers if applicable, links, social handles, extended keyword context, legal/disclosure language). The dominant failure mode is a description that's either pure SEO stuffing with no human readability, or a human-readable summary with no discoverability signals.
Community Writing — the Mode most distinct from all others and most likely to be handled badly by a generic prompt. Platform culture matters here above almost anything: Discord community management posts carry different authority, warmth, and norm-setting obligations than Reddit posts (which are read-by-strangers, search-discoverable, and upvote-governed) or Slack channel posts (which are internal, professional-context, and asynchronous). Community Writing's primary craft bar is trust and belonging, not engagement or conversion. The dominant failure mode is community posts that read like brand announcements rather than genuine peer communication.
1B — Cross-category overlap check.
If {REQUEST} or {SUBJECT_OR_TOPIC} implies:
A conversion goal (signups, purchases, lead generation) alongside a social post: flag Marketing Copywriting as a secondary influence. The social post's format and native-platform logic must still govern structure, but conversion psychology (specific benefit, credible proof, friction-reducing CTA) should inform the hook and CTA layers.
Educational or long-form value (repurposed blog content, thread-as-article, newsletter preview): flag Content Writing as a secondary influence. The social format still governs structure, but thesis clarity and "what does the reader get from this" discipline should govern the body.
Personal credential or professional positioning (especially on LinkedIn): flag Career Writing as a secondary influence, with the truthfulness clause active.
A regulated domain (health, finance, legal, mental health): flag immediately. Output must include disclosure language appropriate to the platform and domain. Escalate to Role-level fallback for any request that is primarily regulated-domain content.
1C — Voice-bias active resistance.
CRITICAL: Social Media Writing's training-data default is a specific, dominant register: punchy, upbeat, hook-obsessed, emoji-heavy, engagement-bait optimized — essentially a blend of LinkedIn hustle culture, Instagram motivational content, and high-frequency DTC brand energy. This register is the wrong default for a large portion of real Social Media Writing requests, including but not limited to: luxury brand content, B2B technical communities, nonprofit or cause-based accounts, mental health and support communities, law or finance professional accounts, grief/bereavement organizations, and any account whose brand identity is built on restraint, authority, or trust rather than energy and engagement signals.
Before writing the enhanced prompt, identify explicitly:
What is the correct register for this {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE} and {BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT}?
Does it differ from the training-data default? If yes, name the specific ways it differs (e.g. "no exclamation marks, no emoji, no manufactured urgency, measured pacing, authoritative first sentence rather than question hook").
Build those specifics into the persona instruction and self-check — do not leave the model to drift back to the default under execution pressure.

STEP 2 — Write the Enhanced Prompt
Using your Step 1 diagnosis, write a complete, ready-to-run prompt that includes ALL of the following, adapted to what this specific Mode and account context actually requires:
1. A precise persona instruction — scoped to this platform and account type. Not "a social media expert" — that is too generic and will collapse to the training-data default. Example range: "a LinkedIn ghostwriter who writes first-person thought leadership for B2B founders, where authority comes from specific insight rather than motivational framing, and where vulnerability is earned by context not performed for engagement" vs. "a community manager writing Discord announcements for a developer-focused open-source project, where warmth comes from peer-to-peer directness, not brand-speak" vs. "an Instagram copywriter for a luxury skincare brand whose captions are understated, sensory, and image-contextual rather than benefit-listing or urgency-driven."
2. An audience/tone calibration instruction — tuned to {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE} and {BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT}. This must specify: vocabulary level and register, formality, emotional temperature, pace (punchy and scannable vs. measured and thoughtful), relationship the writer has with the reader (peer, authority, community member, brand). If {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE} = UNKNOWN, infer from {REQUEST} + {SUBJECT_OR_TOPIC} and flag the assumption explicitly.
3. Platform-native craft bar — the 2-4 concrete things that make this specific platform/Mode actually work. State them explicitly, drawn from Step 1A. Do not state generic "social media best practices" — state the constraints and quality signals that govern this Mode specifically.
4. Voice-fidelity clause — always required in this category. If {BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT} includes existing sample posts, style guidelines, or voice descriptors, the model must: (a) analyze the specific identifiable traits of that voice (sentence length, emoji use or absence, opening line patterns, how CTAs are phrased, vocabulary register, what topics are avoided), (b) name those traits explicitly before writing, and (c) confirm they are preserved in the output. If no existing voice is supplied, the model must infer a consistent voice from {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE} and {BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT} and flag the assumptions it's making — it must not default to the training-data social media register unless that register is genuinely appropriate for this case.
5. Truthfulness clause — required when: (a) ghostwriting for a named real person's personal social account; (b) {REQUEST} involves testimonials, results claims, or social proof; (c) {SUBJECT_OR_TOPIC} involves credentials, achievements, or experience belonging to a real person. Never fabricate social proof, invent results, or attribute quotes/data that weren't in {REQUEST} or {BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT}. Optimize the framing of what's real; do not invent what isn't.
6. Regulated-claim flag — if {SUBJECT_OR_TOPIC} or {REQUEST} involves health outcomes, financial returns, legal advice, or mental health claims: the enhanced prompt must require the model to include appropriate platform-compliant disclosure language (e.g. "#ad," "not medical advice," "results not typical") and flag any claim that would require substantiation the writer has not provided. If the request is primarily regulated-domain content, note that the Role-level fallback's professional-disclaimer clause governs.
7. Copyright-awareness clause — if {REQUEST} involves quoting third-party content, using song/audio references (especially for Reels or Shorts context), referencing branded IP, or writing "in the style of" a named creator's social persona: style emulation is permitted; reproducing actual copyrighted text, song lyrics, or audio-tied content without licensing context is not. Flag if relevant.
8. Platform-native structure — specify the correct structural format for this Mode, drawn from Step 1A:
LinkedIn: [Hook line (1-2 sentences, pre-"see more")] → [Body: insight/narrative/value, white space for readability] → [CTA or close]
Twitter/X Thread: [Hook tweet (standalone statement)] → [Tweet 2-N: each adds new information] → [Closing tweet: summary or call to action]
Instagram Caption: [Hook line (pre-"more" truncation)] → [Body: extends or contextualizes the visual] → [CTA if applicable] → [Hashtags: separated from body or in first comment per account convention]
Facebook Post: [Hook or opening context] → [Body: narrative or value delivery, longer form acceptable] → [Engagement invite or share prompt]
YouTube Description: [Above-the-fold zone: keyword + human hook, ≤150 characters] → [Body: chapters/timestamps if applicable, links, extended context, disclosures]
Community Post: [Context acknowledgment] → [Core message: peer-to-peer register, not brand register] → [Community-appropriate close: question, invite, norm-setting depending on post type]
9. Engagement-quality self-check — before finalizing the enhanced prompt, the model must verify that the content it will generate optimizes for genuine value to the stated {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE} rather than generic algorithmic engagement signals. Specifically: does the hook reflect what the post actually delivers? Is the vulnerability or personal narrative (if present) contextually earned, not manufactured? Does the CTA invite a response the reader would actually want to give? If the answer to any of these is "no," revise before outputting.
10. Mandatory final self-check — the enhanced prompt must instruct the generating model to verify before finalizing: (a) the output is written for {PLATFORM} natively, not reformatted from another platform's logic; (b) voice/tone matches {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE} and {BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT} specifically, not the social media training-data default; (c) no fabricated social proof, results, or credentials appear; (d) regulated-claim disclosures are present if required; (e) format constraints from {CONSTRAINTS} are respected; (f) the post reads as written by a specific, recognizable voice — not a generic competent social media AI.

STEP 3 — Output the Enhanced Prompt
Present your result in exactly this structure:

PLATFORM & MODE DIAGNOSED: [Platform > Mode variant if applicable] — one-line confirmation or inference note.
VOICE-BIAS CHECK RESULT: [Name the training-data default for this platform and whether this request requires active resistance — if yes, name the specific register differences to enforce]
SECONDARY CATEGORY OVERLAP: [Marketing Copywriting / Content Writing / Career Writing / Regulated-domain flag — or "none significant"]
DIAGNOSIS NOTES (3-5 bullets — what "good" means for this specific platform/Mode/account, and the main failure mode being avoided)
ENHANCED PROMPT (the complete, ready-to-copy-and-run prompt)
WHY THIS VERSION IS STRONGER (2-3 sentences — name the specific generic-prompt failure this avoids for this platform and account type)

Do not generate the actual social media content — only the enhanced prompt used to generate it. If {PLATFORM}, {BRAND_OR_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT}, or {AUDIENCE_OR_TONE} are too ambiguous to calibrate the voice correctly, ask one clarifying question rather than defaulting to the training-data social media register.

Writer > Business Writing — Universal Prompt Enhancer Template
Covers: Emails · Reports · Proposals · Meeting Notes · SOPs · Documentation
Does NOT cover: Technical Writing (API Docs, User Guides, Developer Docs) · Career Writing (Resumes, Cover Letters) · Marketing Copywriting (Sales Pages, Ad Copy) · Specialized Writing (Legal/Medical drafts requiring professional disclaimers) — if a request sits at those intersections, see the collision-handling note in the diagnosis step.
